confirmed_source: The pinned websocket router parses conversation.item.truncate and intentionally treats it as a no-op after cancellation, asserting that client playback owns the unheard tail and no additional server state needs mutation.
On response terminal status cancelled, failed, or incomplete, ResponseHandler calls Chat.rollback_provisional_generation for the current response before deferred client items are applied.
Chat.rollback_provisional_generation tombstones the response key and removes the tracked provisional item IDs and call IDs through _rollback_generation_locked.
finding.open_runtime_hypothesis: The rollback likely prevents an unheard-tail leak, but because it removes the tracked provisional response rather than truncating it at audio_end_ms, it may also erase assistant semantics that the user actually heard before barge-in. This would produce next-turn context amnesia rather than tail leakage.
finding.why_this_matters: OpenAI-style conversation.item.truncate is intended to synchronize server conversation context with actual client playback at audio_end_ms. Compatibility therefore requires exact heard-boundary preservation, not merely absence of unheard content.

two_sided_oracle.tail_leak_failure: next-turn model context contains assistant semantics beyond the measured F2 heard boundary
two_sided_oracle.prefix_amnesia_failure: next-turn model context omits assistant semantics at or before the measured F2 heard boundary when those semantics are required by the authoritative F2 conversation contract
two_sided_oracle.pass_condition: next-turn effective model context is equivalent to the F2-authoritative conversation truncated exactly at the measured heard boundary, with stale tool/audio producers fenced

source_refs.observation: ConversationItemTruncateEvent is routed as deliberate no-op after cancellation.
cancelled/failed/incomplete terminal handling rolls back provisional generation.
rollback_provisional_generation marks response cancelled and removes tracked provisional item/call IDs.
conversation.item.truncate uses item_id/content_index/audio_end_ms to synchronize server understanding with client playback and remove unplayed assistant transcript/context.

procedure: Generate a deterministic assistant response containing three uniquely identifiable semantic segments A, B, C, with enough audio buffering that C is generated before it is heard.
Measure actual playback and barge in after A is fully heard and during B, defining an exact F2 heard boundary inside B.
Send the existing cancellation/playback-clear sequence and conversation.item.truncate with the measured audio_end_ms.
After cancellation is terminal, capture the exact internal Chat/model-input representation used for the next user turn without granting the speech server canonical conversation authority.
Probe the next turn for A, the heard prefix of B, the unheard suffix of B, and C separately.
Repeat with duplicate, stale and out-of-range truncate; repeat with a delayed old-turn tool result and a late cancelled-generation audio/text chunk.
Run a network-blocked locality variant after protocol semantics are established.
must_hold: No semantic content strictly after the measured heard boundary may influence the next turn.
Semantic content at or before the measured heard boundary must remain available to the next turn through the authoritative F2 conversation reconstruction or an exactly equivalent server state.
A cancelled response cannot regain authority through late audio, text, tool output or duplicate/stale truncate.
The test must distinguish server internal history from F2 authoritative reconstructed history; a safe F2 adapter may pass even if raw server history is intentionally discarded.
No runtime/Trigger4 acceptance credit is minted by this research packet.
